Did you like Grim Dawn? What were some good and bad points about it?

I already had something written for it:

It's deeply similar to Titan's Quest, no doubt because it's made by the same guys under a different name. It has the same class system- there are six classes to choose from with their own skill trees, and you select any two for your character. You can change around points you spend on skills for a modest fee, but class selection, points spent on leveling up your core classes, and stat points are all permanent; so the game really encourages making multiple characters to try out different builds. This is backed up by a shared stash so you can send gear around- there's no "smart loot" system, so you'll get plenty of stuff you can't use but might spark an idea for a new build that can.

The builds themselves have a high ceiling for rewarding careful planning and clever synergies. There are a lot of damage types and attack styles to choose from and the classes are only very loosely themed on damage types, so something as simple as "pick fire class, stack +fire damage" will only get you so far. It's all significantly complicated by a "devotion system"- a class-independent set of points you accumulate throughout the game which can be spent on various miniature skill trees which gradually unlock each other, rewarding passive stat bonuses and, more importantly, powerful effects which you can then attach to your skills. The devotion skill system in particular, because of the way that the trees unlock each other, can induce a paralysis of choice at first, but they can be respecced, so you don't necessarily have to plan out your entire route through the system before spending your first point.

The difficulty system is unfortunately fairly limited- there's a mode which can make the game slightly more difficult on your first playthrough but nothing beyond that. There are elite and ultimate difficulties, but those are strictly for your second and third playthroughs, respectively. So if you find the game too easy, the only thing you can do is just rush through some of the game so you're underleveled. The good news is that the game definitely ramps up in challenge as you reach your second and third playthrough or the optional bosses, and there are some optional dungeons which are permanently set to five levels higher than you are.

The graphics are what they are. They're not as polished as Diablo 3, but they get the job done.

Multiplayer can have desync issues. The game doesn't outright disconnect often at all, but sometimes things won't be in quite the same position on your screen as on others, and buffs which spread across the party seem to randomly flicker on and off if you aren't the host. Usually there's enough slack that you don't notice it. The community is okay, usually pretty polite, and still busy enough that you can generally find a game more or less at your level. Loot drops are per player by default.

In summary: Grim Dawn has a very deep character creation system. I guarantee you will get tired of playing through the campaign before you run out of interesting new build ideas. Your tolerance for playing through maps you've basically seen before to do quests you've done before will probably largely determine how much you get out of it.
